extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, area/PC chairs, and editors involved with *ACL conferences (ACL, NAACL, EACL) and the TACL journal
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and evaluation guidance for anonymized submission, reviewer behavior, and citation expectations used by *ACL conferences and the TACL journal (covers submission anonymization rules, reviewer conduct, and citation/comparison norms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for anonymized submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: *ACL conferences and TACL require that submissions be anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will not be considered anonymized if authors post (or update) a non-anonymized preprint version within the anonymity period. Submissions will be rejected if not properly anonymized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity period definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity period: from 1 month before the submission deadline until the time of notification (or withdrawal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this period non-anonymized preprints posted by authors make the submission non-anonymized; the rule affects whether a submission is considered properly anonymized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of preprints posted before the anonymity period
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-anonymized preprints posted before the anonymity period are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although allowed, authors are encouraged to wait to post them until after the anonymity period. If such a non-anonymized preprint exists, authors must declare its existence at submission time, should not cite it in the submission, and are asked not to publicize it further during the anonymity period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized preprints allowed during anonymity period
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized preprints within the anonymity period are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is currently only possible on certain platforms; ACL may consider using such a platform for all submissions in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed updates to preprints for name corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL explicitly allows updates to preprints, at all times, for the sole purpose of correcting people's names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a change falls within the anonymity period of a conference, the PC Chairs should be notified of the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad definition of preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprint is understood broadly to refer to any non-refereed paper posted online, including but not limited to preprint servers such as arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule applies only to preprints that authors post themselves, so it does not apply to (for example) non-refereed proceedings volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on updating to prevent 'flag planting'
rubrics_metrics.description: The restriction on updating preprints is intended to prevent authors from circumventing anonymization rules by 'flag planting' with a placeholder version over 1 month in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid using updates to preprints as a way to signal or circumvent anonymity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: do not actively discover author identities
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve double-blind review, reviewers should be instructed not to actively try to discover the identity of the authors and not to let any suspicion or knowledge of author identity affect their judgment of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not prevent reviewers from searching for related work, but they should take special care and postpone such searches until after they have read the paper completely and formed an initial impression of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer protocol when identity is uncovered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer nevertheless uncovers the identity of the authors (or believes they can identify the authors for other reasons), they should inform the area chair or action editor (but not other reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure allows the information to be taken into account when making the final acceptance decision; reviewers should not discuss identities with peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disclosure of outside knowledge (post-Jan 12, 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: After January 12, 2024, ACL reviewing procedures will explicitly ask reviewers to disclose any outside knowledge they may have about a submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosures will be taken into account when assigning and using reviews; reviewers should report relevant outside knowledge when requested by the reviewing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to cite and credit all relevant prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted should in principle cite and compare to all relevant prior work, regardless of when and how that work was presented to the community, and must credit work that influenced them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cite relevant prior work or failure to compare to (non-contemporaneous) empirical results may affect assessment of a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of refereed publications over preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: For citation, refereed publications take priority over preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to cite all refereed publications relevant to their submission, but may be excused for not knowing about unpublished work (especially recently posted or not widely cited preprints). If a preprint has been superseded by a refereed publication, the refereed publication should be cited in addition to or instead of the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling contemporaneous work (less than 3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers appearing less than 3 months before the submission deadline should be considered contemporaneous to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are relieved from the obligation to make detailed comparisons that require additional experimentation and/or in-depth analysis, but are still expected to cite and discuss contemporaneous work to the degree feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer treatment of missing citations to recent preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should give authors the benefit of the doubt in cases where the work appears in preprints with no corresponding refereed publication, especially preprints that are recent and/or not widely cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, reviewers should point authors to the non-cited work (so authors can discuss it in the camera-ready version) but should not penalize the authors for missing the citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic incentives for reviewer quality (May 2025 recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL adopted a recommendation to systematically provide incentives for great reviewers, i.e., implement an ACL Conference Reviewer Awards Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the referenced Reviewer Awards Policy for details; this is a community-level mechanism to recognize high-quality reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol for handling deeply problematic reviewers (May 2025 recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL adopted a recommendation to create a clear protocol for handling deeply problematic reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Peer Review Committee report for details on the protocol; this establishes procedures for addressing severe reviewer misconduct or poor behavior.
